comment: Ep105 Argentina vs England — THE SEMIFINAL. SPECIAL non-template episode. Theme = 'THE GHOSTS OF THE SPOT / DESTINY & THE CURSE BROKEN'. Messi scores BOTH Argentina goals -> wins the GOLDEN BOOT (top scorer) but loses; Kane and Bellingham score England's two. lines.text: Some rivalries aren't decided on grass. They are haunted. And no two nations drag more ghosts onto a football pitch than Argentina and England.
Nineteen eighty-six. Maradona beat England twice in four minutes — the Hand of God, then the greatest goal the World Cup had ever seen.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends. Argentina, versus England — a World Cup semifinal, with forty years of ghosts standing on the touchline.
Two of the greatest teams alive walk into the fire. One will reach the final. The other goes home with the ghosts.
Argentina. The world champions. Blue and white, and a number ten who still bends time itself.
Lionel Messi. The captain, number ten. The heir to Maradona, chasing the one crown his country still dreams of.
And Julian Alvarez, number nine — relentless, fearless, always alive in the box.
England. In white, and finally without fear — a golden generation carrying half a century of hurt.
Harry Kane, the captain, number nine. England's greatest ever goalscorer, still hunting his first great trophy.
And Jude Bellingham, number ten — the young king, born for nights exactly like this one.
Because here is the ghost that will not rest. Nineteen ninety-eight — these same two nations, level at two each, decided on penalties.
Argentina won that shootout. Beckham was sent off. And England's penalty curse — ninety, ninety-eight, two thousand six, a Euro final — was born.
So here is our story. A semifinal that refuses to breathe — two giants trading blow for blow.
England strike first. Kane, ice in his veins, buries it — one, nil to the white shirts.
But the ghost of Maradona wears number ten tonight. Messi answers in a heartbeat — one, all.
England again. Bellingham, the young king, rises highest and heads it home — two, one.
Deep into the night, Argentina throw everyone forward, every prayer aimed at their captain.
And Messi delivers again. His second of the night — two, all — and this semifinal will not be settled in ninety minutes.
Two goals for Messi. The Golden Boot all but his — the tournament's top scorer, echoing Maradona in eighty-six.
But eighty-six is only half the ghost. The other half waits on the penalty spot — where England have died so many times before.
Two, two, after extra time. And this World Cup semifinal — exactly like nineteen ninety-eight — will be decided from twelve yards.
The shootout. The very stage where England's hearts have been broken again, and again, and again.
Kick for kick, nerve for nerve. Messi scores. Kane scores. Nobody blinks.
And then — the save. The England keeper flies, and an Argentine penalty is turned away.
It comes down to one kick. One kick to break a curse that has haunted England for a generation.
He steps up. He strikes. And the net bulges — England win the shootout, four to three!
The curse is broken. England, at last, win on penalties — and march into the World Cup final.
And there, in the storm of English joy, stands Messi. Two goals. The Golden Boot. And no final.
The greatest scorer of the whole tournament — beaten by the one weapon his own country once used to break English hearts. A shootout.
Our prediction — Argentina two, England two. England win four to three on penalties. Messi takes the Golden Boot; England take the final. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
So you tell me. Does England finally bury the ghost — or does Messi's Argentina find one last miracle? Comment ENGLAND, or comment ARGENTINA.
And tonight's legend is the oldest English dream of all. A sword locked in stone, waiting for the one true king to draw it free.
Excalibur. The blade of destiny. The once-and-future king, returned at the very hour England needed him — the curse lifted, the sword drawn at last.
Legend one-zero-five. Excalibur — because some nights, destiny simply stops waiting.
Here's how you claim it. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds — and Excalibur, Legend one-zero-five, is yours.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for glory.
So claim your Legend, and send this to a friend who still believes in destiny. Hit like, hit subscribe, and I'll see you at the final.
